Control the size of the smallest level in the Multi-Band blending pyramid. Smaller values of suppression increase the number of pyramid levels, which in turn can help balancing the differences in colour and exposure between images. On the other hand, larger values of suppression result in less pyramid levels, thus the result would be similar to an Alpha blend.

Select the image blending method.
Alpha - Merge images using the alpha channels.
Multi-Band - Merge images at different scales.
Spherical Multi-Band - As above but in spherical domain.

Set the output mode for the individual camera views.
Unwarped - Pass-through the input on each view, a stitch map layer will be generated in each camera view.
Warped - Apply global warp deformation on each view.

Set the projection type for the individual camera views.
Default - Pass-through the input on each view.
Spherical - Project each camera to the output panorama.

This is the GPU that will be used for rendering, when Use GPU if available is selected. If you have more than one GPU in your machine, you can select a different GPU Device to use by editing your Preferences. (Note that selecting a different GPU will require a restart of Nuke to take effect.) Local GPU will be shown as Not available when any of the following is true: * Use CPU is selected as the GPU Device in your Preferences. * No suitable GPU was found on your system. Please refer to the documentation for details of the requirements for GPU acceleration. * It was not possible to create a context for processing on the selected GPU. For example, this can happen when there is not enough free memory available on the GPU. To use the GPU when rendering from the command line, add --gpu to your command.

Use this to control the size of the grid that will be used to warp each camera view. Decrease the size to generate more regular warps. Increase the size to generate more detailed warps. node = nuke.thisNode() 
node['licenseCheckTrigger'].execute() 
proceed = bool(node['licenseCheckResult'].getValue()) 
if proceed: 
  matched = node['isMatched'].getValue() 
  if matched: 
    proceed = nuke.ask('Proceeding will reset the existing camera matches. Are you sure?') 
if proceed: 
  node['executeType'].setValue(0) 
  keysKnob = node['analysisKeyframe'] 
  if keysKnob.getNumKeys() == 0: 
    keysKnob.setKeyAt(min(max(nuke.frame(), node.firstFrame()), node.lastFrame())) 
  indexRange = range(0, keysKnob.getNumKeys()) 
  frameRange = nuke.FrameRanges([int(keysKnob.getKeyTime(k)) for k in indexRange]) 
  nuke.execute(node, frameRange)

default.value:
node = nuke.thisNode() 
node['licenseCheckTrigger'].execute() 
proceed = bool(node['licenseCheckResult'].getValue()) 
firstFrame = node.firstFrame() 
lastFrame = node.lastFrame() 
trackingStep = int(node['trackingStep'].getValue()) 
startFrame = int(node['constraintStartFrame'].getValue()) 
endFrame = int(node['constraintEndFrame'].getValue()) 
if proceed and startFrame == endFrame: 
  p = nuke.Panel('Enter tracking range') 
  p.addSingleLineInput('from:', str(firstFrame)) 
  p.addSingleLineInput('to:', str(lastFrame)) 
  p.addSingleLineInput('step:', str(trackingStep)) 
  ret = p.show() 
  if ret: 
    try: 
      startFrame = int(p.value('from:')) 
      endFrame = int(p.value('to:')) 
      trackingStep = int(p.value('step:')) 
      node['constraintStartFrame'].setValue(startFrame) 
      node['constraintEndFrame'].setValue(endFrame) 
      node['trackingStep'].setValue(trackingStep) 
    except ValueError: 
      nuke.message('Invalid range values') 
      proceed = False 
  else: 
    proceed = False 
if proceed: 
  node['executeType'].setValue(3) 
  nuke.execute(node, firstFrame, lastFrame)

Select this to render on the Local GPU, if available. You can select this even if no GPU is currently available on your machine. If this node requires full frames from its inputs, and is therefore unable to reduce its memory overhead, it will fall back to the CPU if an attempt to render a frame on the GPU fails due to lack of memory. When this occurs, a warning message will be printed to the console.

description.plain_text: C_GlobalWarp 2.1v5: Analyse and correct input footage from a rig using the camera metadata to minimise the ghosting in the overlapping regions. The correction is based on the camera matches, which are used to find the best grid warp transformation of each input footage at the given convergence depth. Keying: Set analysis keys where there is structure and/or a depth change in the overlap region between images. Analysis: Control the warping process. Analyse the sequence to find the camera matches at the analysis keys, and then warp to align the input footage. You can add new keys anytime, and compute the camera matches at those keys only. Settings: Control the parameters underpinning the warping process. Line Constraints: Constraints can be added to keep lines straight during the warping. Create as many line constraints as needed. Add the constraint keys to the analysis keys. Optionally compute camera matches at the new keys. Finally update the warp. Output: The stitched panorama is shown in the main view. Set the output format, blend type, and resampling filter to render the final panorama. Each camera view will show the input footages. If the camera views are unwarped a stitch map layer will also be provided.
description.text:
C_GlobalWarp 2.1v5: Analyse and correct input footage from a rig using the camera metadata to minimise the ghosting in the overlapping regions. The correction is based on the camera matches, which are used to find the best grid warp transformation of each input footage at the given convergence depth.

Keying: Set analysis keys where there is structure and/or a depth change in the overlap region between images.

Analysis: Control the warping process. Analyse the sequence to find the camera matches at the analysis keys, and then warp to align the input footage. You can add new keys anytime, and compute the camera matches at those keys only.

Settings: Control the parameters underpinning the warping process.

Line Constraints: Constraints can be added to keep lines straight during the warping. Create as many line constraints as needed. Add the constraint keys to the analysis keys. Optionally compute camera matches at the new keys. Finally update the warp.

Output: The stitched panorama is shown in the main view. Set the output format, blend type, and resampling filter to render the final panorama. Each camera view will show the input footages. If the camera views are unwarped a stitch map layer will also be provided.
